newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends weaker but well-off lows.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends weaker but well-off lows.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures settled a heavily-traded session lower, but trade scale-down buying held the October contract above nearby support and buoyed prices off the lows by the close, market sources said.

The bulk of the day's losses came after October sank through support at 11.50 on early speculative liquidation. The contract reached its low of 11.30, consolidated, and then gradually retraced some losses.

The early selling also weighed heavily on the most-active March contract, which fell through a double-bottom on the charts at 11.35. The October/March spread closed at 0.15, barely changed from 0.16 on Monday's close.

Additional selling is likely to come into the March contract since speculators have already rolled a hefty number of positions from October, ahead of the contract's expiry later this month, dealers said.
Open interest in March stood at 62,145, off 953 as of Monday. Open interest in October stood at 41,308, off 10,139.
October sank 0.14 on the day to close at 11.43, having traded from 11.52 to 11.30. March ended off 0.13 at 11.28, while the back months settled off 0.08 to 0.06.
Volume was estimated at a brisk 45,555 lots.
Dealers pegged October resistance between 11.50 and 11.60.
Refco analyst Ann Prendergast said the market appears poised to head lower, "but certainly is in no hurry to do so."
She said the market skirted the huge plunge in prices expected from a seasonal lull and a record Brazilian crop, since high domestic prices kept the bulk of sugar in Brazil.
"Prices weakend some and they still have more to go, but I'm a bit cautious about reaching 11.00," Prendergast said.

LIFFE white sugar futures also settled down sharply, with losses in New York contributing to weakness in London. Spot December finished $5.40 lower to $327.00. The back months ended $4.70 to $2.20 lower.
